text:
anya: heads up - in the canary rollout view I'm seeing p99 lower than p50 for /v1/generate in eu-west, which is impossible unless something odd is happening :confused:
kevin: can you paste the numbers?
anya: sure, slice=canary-0.2 -> p50=115ms, p95=117ms, p99=88ms (from the dashboard)
morgan: wild. Either the samples aren't the same population or units got mixed during merge
taylor: did we recently change any tags or provenance labels on ingest? could be client vs server timing collapsed into one series
anya: I queried the raw series and got two distinct origins: transport_ms (unit=ms) and backend_proc (unit=s). backend_proc samples are like 0.088 which the rollup converted to 88 (assumed ms)
kevin: so backend_proc in seconds ended up being interpreted as ms. When tdigest merges those differently scaled samples, quantiles can invert due to weighting differences
morgan: conclusion: we must not merge across different unit tags without normalizing. We should either normalize during ingest or refuse to merge and surface a warning in the UI
taylor: UX side: dashboard currently just shows the number; product will panic seeing p99 drop in a canary. We should show a provenance indicator on pctl lines and an explicit "mixed-units" warning that expands to explain the issue
anya: suggested short-term fixes:
- kevin: add ingestion normalizer for latency metrics (if unit=="s", multiply by 1000) and emit a metadata tag "unit_normalized" (PR target: today)
- morgan: add a backend check to block tdigest merges when unit tag is missing/conflicting and mark series as "merge_blocked"
- taylor: add console tooltip + badge for quantile provenance and a quick toggle so rollouts compare "same-origin-only" by default for pctl charts
- metrics-bot: schedule a cronjob that scans for quantile inversion (p99 < p50) and posts a summary daily to #eng-platform-incidents
kevin: implementation note: some legacy sources omit unit tag. For those, we can infer by distribution (if median < 5 then probably seconds vs ms?) but label them as "unit_inferred" instead of trusted
morgan: +1 on inference with annotation. Also add a small sanity check in the rollup pipeline that rejects merges if max(sample)/min(sample) > 1000 and unit tag absent
taylor: for the rollout UX, instead of hiding pctl values, show a red warning icon next to the metric and offer a clickable modal that lists contributing sample origins and their units
anya: metrics-bot: quick scan please?
metrics-bot: automated-scan: in the last 24h found 4 slices with p99 < p50. First example: endpoint=/v1/generate slice=canary-0.2 region=eu-west (matches above)
kevin: I'll open the normalizer PR and add unit inference logic in a separate follow-up; will ping when in staging
morgan: thanks -- this explains the weird canary alerts from yesterday. Good catch, Anya. :thumbsup:
taylor: I'll prototype the provenance badge mockups and share a link later today
anya: adding this to the incident doc and closing the loop once the PR lands. Good work everyone.
